figures: 1. Figure 1: Generated samples from our adaptive dual-scale diffusion model across different runs and datasets. Each row represents a different experimental run, while columns show results for circle, dino, line, and moons datasets.

2. Figure 2: Evolution of global and local feature weights across timesteps for different datasets. The x-axis represents timesteps (from end to beginning of the diffusion process), while the y-axis shows weight values. Each line represents the weight for global (solid) and local (dashed) features for a specific dataset.
results_section: 1. The final model with the improved weight network (Run 5) achieves the following improvements over the baseline: Circle: 2.5% reduction (from 0.354 to 0.345)
2. The final model with the improved weight network (Run 5) achieves the following improvements over the baseline: Dino: 12.8% reduction (from 0.989 to 0.862)
3. The final model with the improved weight network (Run 5) achieves the following improvements over the baseline: Line: 5.0% reduction (from 0.161 to 0.153)
4. The final model with the improved weight network (Run 5) achieves the following improvements over the baseline: Moons: 3.3% improvement (from 0.090 to 0.093)
5. Training times approximately doubled, from an average of 36.97 seconds for the baseline to 75.19 seconds for the final model across all datasets.
6. We observed reductions in KL divergence across all datasets, with the most substantial improvement of 12.8% observed in the complex dino dataset.
